## Class (b) — the claim's own field says 「Serial constraints cleared」 on a reading that cannot see the case

The seat's `Claim:` template (every claim this shift, e.g. 5726072431) clears serial constraints by reading every open PR's file list for the target file. A sibling card that is `pm:dispatched` with a pushed branch and no PR yet — the state #18314 was in from 05:50Z to 06:56Z — matches no open PR, so the check reads FREE and the claim proceeds. Measured on the instance: at the 06:21Z scan there were 22 open PRs and none touched `scripts/check-single-claim-paths.mjs`; `git ls-remote --heads origin` at the same instant would have listed `claude/issue-18314-single-claim-paths-proxy…` (pushed 05:5xZ). AGENTS.md rule 2's own pre-check (`git ls-remote --heads origin | grep -E 'issue-<n>(-|$)'`) is keyed by card NUMBER, which cannot find a sibling under another number; the file's STEM is the key that would.

## Done when (⛔ a proposal, measure)

- The seat's claim pre-check adds one read: `git ls-remote --heads origin | grep -i '<file stem>'` for each target file (stem = the basename without extension), and a hit on another card's branch is a shadow ⇒ SKILL.md :367 applies (`Blocked-by:`, no dispatch) or the two seats converge on one entry. Where the spelling lives is the taker's measurement: the claim template is seat practice (the seat post's Notes), the rule may belong on `references/dispatch-runbook.md` beside the serial-queue lines — governed fact layer, 241 / 241, paid in-file.
- Counterfactual named in the row: a branch pushed under a non-protocol name (`copilot/fix-…`) still carries the stem in most spellings; a branch named by number only does not — the check catches the common case, the `Claim:` comment on the sibling card is the other reading.
